Latest Update: Mammograms May Offer Early Insight Into Cardiovascular Disease

📅 08 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (817 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mammograms are widely used to help detect breast cancer, but they may also offer insight into heart health.
  • The routine X-ray screening may identify breast arterial calcification (BAC), which is the presence of calcium deposits within the walls of the small arteries in the breast.
  • On a mammogram, BAC is commonly identified as thin, white, parallel lines that give a “tram-track” appearance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mammograms are widely used to help detect breast cancer, but they may also offer insight into heart health.

The routine X-ray screening may identify breast arterial calcification (BAC), which is the presence of calcium deposits within the walls of the small arteries in the breast.

On a mammogram, BAC is commonly identified as thin, white, parallel lines that give a “tram-track” appearance.

While BAC is harmless to the breasts, it is associated with a significantly higher risk of cardiovascular disease. A 2022 study found women with BAC were 51% more likely to develop heart disease or experience a stroke than those without it.

Industry observers note that laxmi Mehta, MD, a cardiologist at The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center, remarked BAC is associated with cardiovascular risk factors, such as diabetes, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol. Additionally, BAC has been connected to:.

“The reasons for BAC resulting in higher risks for cardiovascular disease are not definitely determined; however, there are some potential mechanisms, one being that they share similar risk factors that result in vascular injury or metabolic stress that result in vascular calcification and atherosclerosis,” Mehta told Healthline.

Cheng-Han Chen, MD, interventional cardiologist and medical director of the Structural Heart Program at MemorialCare Saddleback Medical Center, added that because BAC and heart disease share many of the same risk factors, “calcium in breast arteries therefore suggests disease in the heart (coronary) and brain arteries as well,” he told Healthline.

While 1 in 39 females in the United States dies from breast cancer each year, cardiovascular disease causes one out of every three deaths, resulting in 1 death per minute.

“Cardiovascular disease is still the most common cause of death in premenopausal women,” Richard Reitherman, MD, PhD, a radiologist and medical director of breast imaging at MemorialCare Breast Center at Orange Coast Medical Center, told Healthline.

“The presentation of cardiovascular disease in premenopausal women is notoriously different than in postmenopausal women, primarily [because] there are no typical symptoms such as chest pain.”.

Reitherman said that a prevalent and common health screening procedure such as a mammogram can lead to the early identification of women with silent cardiovascular disease.

“Cardiovascular outcome studies that have included breast arterial calcifications as a risk factor are increasingly reported in the medical literature,” he said.

“The hope is that identifying younger women with silent cardiovascular risks [like BAC along with] appropriate integrated risk identification, analysis, and interventions can significantly reduce mortality in this age group.”.

Mehta stated there are several reasons BAC has been overlooked as a risk factor for heart disease.

“Mammograms are completed for assessment of breast cancer, and BAC has been historically an ‘incidental’ finding, which is not clinically relevant from an oncologic standpoint,” she remarked.

Additionally, there is no standardization on quantification of BAC severity, nor is it a required component of mammogram reports, said Mehta.

However, routine reporting of BAC on mammograms is an urgent goal of the American College of Radiology, Society of Breast Imaging, and Medicare, stated Reitherman.

In fact, it is gaining traction in the United States. A new Maryland law, passed on October 1, requires mammography centers to notify women when a BAC is detected on their mammogram.

“Automated identification and reporting of these calcifications detected on screening mammograms will become increasingly prevalent in the coming months [and] years,” remarked Reitherman.

The next step is to identify this group of women to primary care physicians so that appropriate risk evaluation can take place, Reitherman added.

In addition to doctors routinely screening for conditions related to heart disease, such as diabetes, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol, he hopes BAC will also be routinely considered.

“Under current development are protocols to identify patients needing a cardiologist’s training and expertise to appropriately stratify this group of patients,” mentioned Reitherman.

“The common healthcare behavior [of] having regular mammograms not only reduces risk of morbidity and mortality from breast cancer but will hopefully contribute to the reduction of morbidity and mortality from cardiovascular disease in younger women.”.

He said this type of integrated healthcare approach demonstrates cross-specialty integration and coordination among women, radiologists, and their healthcare providers to improve women’s lives.

“This is an amazing game-changing opportunity,” Reitherman said.

Mehta said it’s reasonable for women to ask if BAC is present on their mammogram report.

“But if it is not uniformly reported by the radiologist, the individual clinician may not have the answer,” she said.

More research is needed before BAC on mammograms can be used routinely to predict heart disease.

Finding out your BAC could provide additional information to help you and your doctors decide how aggressively to address your cardiovascular risk factors, Chen said.

In a recent development, reitherman agreed. “The goal of reducing morbidity and mortality from any cause such as cardiovascular disease is based on recognition of risk factors, followed by appropriate lifestyle and pharmacologic interventions,” he mentioned.

The Overlooked Social Origins of Machiavellian Behavior

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1212 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated November 26, 2026 | Reviewed by Kaja Perina.
  • In a recent development, in 1532, statesman Niccolo Machiavelli's book The Prince was published across Renaissance Italy.
  • Many philosophers before and after Machiavelli emphasized people as having a self-interested nature.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 26, 2026 | Reviewed by Kaja Perina.

In a recent development, in 1532, statesman Niccolo Machiavelli's book The Prince was published across Renaissance Italy. While controversial, his magnum opus on statecraft was widely deemed innovative for de-emphasizing ethical norms and ultra-pragmatically explaining what leaders should do to hold and gain power.

Many philosophers before and after Machiavelli emphasized people as having a self-interested nature. Like him, they often emerged from ceaselessly unstable, war-prone milieus. Legalists from ancient China viewed Confucians as too morally idealistic; early modern England's Thomas Hobbes held a dimmer view of human nature than did John Locke. Yet, it was the term "Machiavellian" that endured and evolved in English writing since the mid-1500s. Today, it refers to being calculated, insincere, and even unprincipled to gain something.

It has been revealed that as a psychological concept, "Machiavellianism" is associated with cynical, manipulative, and self-serving tendencies. Psychologists have even measured it through scales like the MACH-IV and Five-Factor Machiavellianism Inventory. Popular articles and videos abound with titles about how to find "narcissists" among partners, or to beware of "dark triad" traits in co-workers. Whether or not they capture phenomenologically valid constructs, or align with how health professionals use these terms, they do not always include structural approaches and takeaways. Could how Machiavellianism presents in societies give clues into broader social issues needing addressing?

People with similar childhood adversities can grow up to have very different worldviews. However, for some, a combination of early deprivations, caregiver modeling, and hereditary factors can increase their likelihood of internalizing cynical outlooks. These could crystallize into enduring, Machiavellian patterns of interaction later on. Early childhood attachment disruptions, relational losses, and conditional, inconsistent affection can contribute to understanding relationships as ultimately transactional. Frequent bullying, abuse, or social injustices without accountability might misguide some to view ethical and, sometimes, institutional rules as naive or frivolous.

In a recent development, later, resulting cravings for "omnipotent control" can lead to great efforts to control how most others view and treat oneself, sometimes in ways contradictory to one's actual self. One applies an astute "theory of mind" for envisioning what others want. Consider a group leader who speaks frequently of uplifting and bringing people together, but privately gossips and plays potential competitors against each other. Or a colleague who cultivates a reputation as a light-hearted jokester, but emotionally abuses their partner at home. Their friends might not believe they have such dissonant traits, let alone have suspected these early on. Indeed, psychoanalysts refer to the superego lacunae of otherwise upstanding people who harbor deeply dark tendencies in specific domains of life.

But how useful is it, really, to focus on the sensationalism, the individual "wrongness" or "pathology," or the developmental roots of Machiavellian characteristics? Nobody denies that manipulation and relational aggression happen. Individuals with such traits--or at least a strong disposition to them--exist in all human societies, but how and to what extent these manifest depends greatly on one's present and future environments.

Historian E.P. Thompson examined the moral economy of everyday Englishmen in the 1700s, focusing on nuanced motivations of bread riots beyond hunger itself. As Thompson's work supported, people may be at least as driven to drastic action--in his examples, selective intimidation and aggression toward middlemen--by perceived violations of what is normatively reasonable and fair, than by economic inequality in and of itself.

It has been revealed that yet, unlike for his early modern examples, vigilante retribution is no longer as tolerated in most societies. "Fighting fire [i.e. injustices] with fire" can nowadays land people in prison, depending on their methods. Cynicism may then simmer if people see widespread violation of implicit norms of fairness without meaningful consequences.

It has been revealed that examples appear painfully difficult for the observer to challenge; they range from deliberate decisions, like leaders' rewarding betrayals of colleagues who find themselves in hard times, to rigidly structural imbalances like co-workers getting overlooked for opportunities due to their ethnicity, gender, or religion. In turn, self-serving, insincere, performative, and manipulative behaviors can become gradually more tolerated, rewarded, and normalized in groups. Generalized trust, authenticity, good-faith charity, and optimism might all slowly wither.

Is it useful to think of widespread Machiavellianism as mutually reinforcing and cyclically associated with greater cynicism in a society? Maybe yes, but that is also not the full picture. Perhaps in most cases, prone to quid pro quo exchanges and transactional alliance-building, Machiavellianism is unlikely to improve social concerns long-term. It would not benefit any group's already low-trust culture, declining public confidence in a given institution, or corruption. If anything, the rewarding of one's playing dirty could encourage more of such tendencies in their circles via social learning.

Sources indicate that yet, for some others, witnessing Machiavellianism's normalization might not transform their personalities overall. It would instead outwardly modify their interpersonal approaches to achieving pre-existing, potentially socially constructive goals. These ends, regardless of their means, go beyond everyday self-preservation and range from improving the marginalized social status of one's group to advancing a specific policy.

Sources indicate that what might such Machiavellian-like adaptation or imitation look like for someone who did not grow up with overtly congruent traits? Examples include adopting more guardedness and suspicion, calculation and self-restraint in what one says and to whom, flattery, selectively concealing one's true feelings, and discreetly discerning colleagues' interests and "agendas." Saying things one does not fully mean or feel may seem advantageous, even encouraged, when one assumes their superiors do the same. One might increasingly rationalize their strategic exploitation of others' misfortunes. If these are the prevailing, implicit rules of engagement in one's organizational or workplace politics, then so they will practice them. As with what Friedrich Nietzsche noted about fighting monsters, they should also take care lest they essentially "become" Machiavellian through and through.

Industry observers note that not every instance of Machiavellianism in one's workplace, organization, or community indicates a structurally sick society. A few individuals, regardless of how much privilege they have, can still demonstrate such features during periods of widespread optimism and trust, even if their tendencies are more the exception than the norm. Conversely, not everyone who has developed a protective cynicism wants to take advantage of others.

That mentioned, how prevalent Machiavellianism is in a group at a given time may hint at underlying competition over resources perceived as both finite and unfairly allocated. Resources are not necessarily just material wealth, but also social capital, status, and power. Underhanded ways of interaction may reflect not just neurodevelopmental predispositions but also, for those who are most angry, disillusioned, or hardened, an instrumental means of efficiently accumulating such resources.

None of this absolves the need for accountability and responsibility for inflicting interpersonal harms. Advocacy can be done primarily through good-faith methods. Leaders can promote workplace cultures that are more fair and transparent than what they knew in the past. Yet, so long as racism, sexism, xenophobia, homophobia, and other social ills persist, Machiavellianism may continue to appear to some a legitimate way of navigating work and life--not just for those seeking to maintain great privilege, but also, and perhaps especially, for many people without much of it.

Series production of the new iX4 is officially underway at BMW Group’s manufacturing plant in Debrecen, Hungary.

The iX4 is the second fully electric BMW model built at the facility, following the record-breaking production ramp-up of the fresh iX3 SUV.

BMW said the plant began series production of an entirely fresh model in less than two months after the company introduced a 24-hour, three-shift schedule to ramp up output to meet higher-than-expected demand.

The new iX4 will go on sale in March 2027 as an all-electric replacement for the X4. It will be available in two variants: the BMW iX4 50 xDrive and BMW iX4 40 xDrive, with a range-topping M60 xDrive set to follow shortly after.

Both versions use a dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain. The iX4 50 xDrive provides a combined 468 hp and 475 lb-ft of torque, enabling it to sprint from 0 to 60 mph in 4.7 seconds.

The performance M60 version delivers a combined 603 hp and 645 lb-ft of torque, which BMW indicates is good for a 0 to 60 mph sprint in just 3.9 seconds.

In a recent development, the iX4 features a distinct coupe-SUV-like silhouette rather than the traditional boxy, upright SUV design of the iX3. With a rakish roofline and an aerodynamic design, the latest iX4 has a drag coefficient of just 0.23.

Like the iX3, the iX4 is based on BMW’s Neue Klasse architecture with its sixth-generation (Gen6) eDrive system.

While EPA figures have yet to be finalized, BMW said the upcoming iX4 has an estimated driving range of up to 428 miles on a single charge using a 112.2 kWh battery. Under WLTP conditions, it offers an all-electric range of up to 514 miles (828 km).

Thanks to its 800V architecture, BMW’s new iX4 can add up to 184 miles of range (384 km on the WLTP cycle) in just 10 minutes with charging speeds of up to 400 kW. Charging the vehicle from 10% to 80% takes about 21 minutes.

Sources indicate that like BMW’s other Neue Klasse models, the latest iX4 features its updated interior design. The setup includes a large 17.9″ infotainment screen and BMW’s new Panoramic Vision, a 42″ display spanning the base of the windshield.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that 18 years after Honda filed the first official airbag recall and 12 years since the first round of mass recalls began, the Takata airbag scandal remains ongoing.
  • The pair of recalls filed in November include a population of more than 1.6 million vehicles.
  • Despite the growing recall population, the core glitch remains generally unchanged from previous Takata recalls.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that 18 years after Honda filed the first official airbag recall and 12 years since the first round of mass recalls began, the Takata airbag scandal remains ongoing. This month, Honda and Toyota have both filed latest recalls with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration related to faulty airbag inflators.

The pair of recalls filed in November include a population of more than 1.6 million vehicles. Late-model Hondas make up over 810,000 units in the recall, while Toyota accounts for 790,000 units, 314,000 of which are located in the United States. NHTSA documents indicate that 2013 Honda Accord, 2012-2013 Honda Civic, 2012-2013 Honda CR-V, 2013 Acura ILX, 2013 Acura RDX models, 2002-2010 Lexus SC430, 2011 ‌IS250, ⁠2017 GX460, 2003-2008 Toyota Corolla, 2005-2006 Tundra, 2005-2007 Sequoia and 2016-2017 4Runner models are included in the recall.

Despite the growing recall population, the core glitch remains generally unchanged from previous Takata recalls. “The airbag inflator propellant can degrade with repeated exposure to high-humidity environments and large temperature variation, resulting in increased internal pressure. If an affected airbag deploys, the increased internal pressure may cause the inflator to rupture (break apart) and deploy abnormally,” NHTSA documents explain. “In the event of an inflator rupture, metal fragments could pass through the airbag cushion material possibly causing serious injury or fatality to vehicle occupants.”.

There have been no injuries or crashes tied to the vehicles being newly recalled. However, NHTSA has recorded 28 deaths in the United States and more than 400 injuries stemming from defective Takata airbag inflators since 2009. The Takata airbag recall remains the largest recall in U.S. history.

It has been revealed that given the rolling nature of the Takata recall, Honda and Toyota were already in discussions with federal regulators when this airbag version began to show signs of degradation. Honda first identified an concern during simulation testing under severe environmental conditions in May 2025. However, these tests didn’t show abnormal inflator behavior or a “statistically significant deviation” from previous prediction models. Similarly, Toyota had been collecting and studying certain Takata inflators since 2016, specifically focusing on a desiccated, phase-stabilized ammonium nitrate (PSAN) propellant. Toyota’s predictive models indicated that some of these inflators could be reaching the end of their life, prompting the Japanese automaker to conduct a voluntary safety recall.

The remedy is fairly simple for both automakers: Toyota and Honda will simply replace the airbag inflators on affected units. Honda says its latest inflators are manufactured by a different supplier and use a different propellant that does not degrade over the long term when exposed to high temperatures, high humidity, and large temperature fluctuations. Either way, both automakers and federal regulators urge affected owners to have their airbag inflators swapped out as soon as possible.

Tesla FSD v15 is AI4’s last shot as Musk reveals how little compute is left

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1631 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla’s FSD v15 is its last real shot at delivering unsupervised self-driving on the AI4 computer in millions of customer cars.
  • He also confirmed that cars won’t get the next-gen AI5 chip, and that the mid-cycle AI4.5 upgrade just had its RAM cut from 32GB to 24GB.
  • The most visible part of FSD v15 is Tesla Reality View, a live, video-game-like rendering of the car’s surroundings with chevrons floating in the sky for upcoming turns.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla’s FSD v15 is its last real shot at delivering unsupervised self-driving on the AI4 computer in millions of customer cars. Elon Musk spent the weekend explaining on X how the new software uses the hardware, and there isn’t much room left.

He also confirmed that cars won’t get the next-gen AI5 chip, and that the mid-cycle AI4.5 upgrade just had its RAM cut from 32GB to 24GB.

The most visible part of FSD v15 is Tesla Reality View, a live, video-game-like rendering of the car’s surroundings with chevrons floating in the sky for upcoming turns. Musk called it “real-time AI video generation (no gaming engine!) using just half of one AI4 TRIP accelerator.”.

Industry observers note that the fan accounts ran with that as a flex. But Musk’s follow-up posts tell a different story.

He explained that after Tesla moved a decoder into SRAM, “we only have half a TRIP out of three on SoC B, for this reality visualizer, so spent the compute as best we could.” In other words, half a TRIP is what was left over. He added that TRIP, Tesla’s neural accelerator, “basically only handles 8-bit int and has to run softmax in emulation mode in 28 steps.”.

In another post, Musk described Reality View as a roughly 1-billion-parameter diffusion model running off the same vision encoder features “that are plugged into the 3B encoder model that produces the driving actions.” He admitted the visualization’s latency is “a bit high due to compute constraints.”.

It has been revealed that that 3B figure is worth noting. Tesla talked up a 10x jump in FSD model size for over a year, first for v14 and then for v15. Musk didn’t say whether 3B covers the entire driving stack, but it’s nowhere near 10x.

And Tesla’s own engineers aren’t describing a chip with lots of headroom. Dilreet Raju, who works on Tesla’s AI silicon, wrote that the hardest work of his life was co-designing the v15 vision encoder “to squeeze out the last few percents of MFU from AI4.” MFU is model FLOPs utilization, a measure of how much of the chip’s theoretical compute the model actually uses. Musk replied with a target emoji.

Industry observers note that when Tesla unveiled its FSD computer in 2019, the selling point was redundancy: two independent chips on one board, each with its own power and memory, so one could take over if the other failed. As we noted when Tesla started shipping the AI4.5 computer in Model Y in January, Tesla’s FSD computers have historically used two identical chips for exactly that reason.

Recent findings suggest that that’s what an unsupervised, Level 4 system needs. With nobody in the driver’s seat, a hardware fault can’t simply hand control back to a human. The car needs enough healthy compute left to keep seeing the road and pull over safely.

But Musk’s own description indicates SoC B running the decoder and the Reality View model, not sitting idle as a mirror of SoC A. Tesla hackers, including greentheonly, have reported for years that Tesla started splitting its FSD workload across both chips back in the HW3 days.

According to recent reports, tesla has never explained how much of AI4 it reserves for failover, or whether a single SoC can run enough of the stack to bring a car to a safe stop on its own. The more of the board v15 needs, the harder that question gets.

Waymo has answered it publicly. The company claims both of its onboard computing systems run full workloads in parallel and that a secondary computer can bring the vehicle to a safe stop if the primary fails, backed by redundant braking, steering and power. Its upcoming custom chip is rated at more than 1,000 TOPS. By our own comparison of AI4 and Nvidia’s Drive Thor, AI4 is estimated at roughly 100 to 150 TOPS across both chips.

Tesla started rolling out FSD v15 on Saturday, claiming “25x better handling of safety critical cases” without any baseline. So far, the people posting videos are mostly the usual crowd of Tesla-focused accounts that get early builds. Just hours before the rollout started, Musk wrote that v15 “goes to wide release next month.”.

According to recent reports, the early clips are almost all about Reality View, the fresh parking spot selection, and the floating arrows. Those are UI features. They say very little about how many miles v15 can drive between critical interventions, which is the only number that matters for unsupervised driving.

That brings us to AI4.5. On Tesla’s Q1 2026 earnings call, Musk revealed an “AI4 Plus” with RAM doubled from 16GB to 32GB per chip, which raised the question of whether HW4 would follow HW3.

This weekend, Musk remarked “AI4.5 is a relatively small performance improvement that is mostly due to needing to upgrade RAM to LPDDR5X.” Hours later, he added: “RAM is super expensive, so we reduced AI4.5 from 32GB to 24GB. That will be fine. It’s hard to use 32GB anyway, given memory bandwidth constraints.”.

He also noted that AI4 “costs twice as much now due to memory and storage price hikes.”.

So the mid-cycle refresh exists mainly because Tesla needs a newer memory type it can actually buy, not to unlock bigger models. If memory bandwidth is the bottleneck, as Musk keeps repeating, adding capacity doesn’t change much.

Industry observers note that asked by an owner on Sunday whether to wait for AI5 before upgrading from HW3, Musk answered: “It’s going to Optimus. Cars will remain at AI4. That’s enough to solve superhuman driving.”.

Sources indicate that an interesting comment, as it destroys one thing that HW3 owners were holding to: Tesla was delaying HW3 upgrades until it had AI5. Now, it’s clearly not the case and Tesla has no excuse not to upgrade HW3 cars.

It has been revealed that he described AI5 as “a gigantic improvement. Roughly 12X more compute,” and later as “roughly an order of magnitude hardware performance improvement, all things considered. Memory bandwidth is a constraint.” Last year, he stated that by some metrics AI5 would be 40 times better than AI4.

AI5 is also moving around. In October, Musk stated Tesla cut AI5’s RAM in half to 72GB to get enough volume for Optimus, then nudged it back up to 96GB a day later. AI6 was cut by a third, to 144GB of LPDDR6. When asked about AI6 this weekend, Musk replied with a chef’s kiss meme.

According to recent reports, as we reported in July, Samsung’s Texas fab won’t reach AI5 volume production until the second half of 2027, nearly two years behind Musk’s original timeline. And that volume is now headed to robots and data centers, not cars.

This is the situation for AI4 owners: v15 has to be the one. And we heard Elon Musk calling every FSD revision “the one” for the last decade.

Tesla’s own engineers are talking about squeezing the last few percent of utilization out of AI4. Musk describes a half-accelerator scrap of compute left for the visualizer. The AI4.5 refresh is a RAM swap that just got downsized, and AI5 isn’t coming to cars. If v15 can’t get to unsupervised driving on AI4, there’s no hardware escape hatch for the fleet.

I seem to remember a couple of years ago Tesla released a significant revision in November, only to encounter chip overheating problems the following summer. Now they are admitting that the old chip is running flat out, that means heat. Heat that they have to get rid of in cars that already are dealing with inadequate cooling.

According to recent reports, we’ve seen this movie before. Tesla said HW3 was enough for unsupervised self-driving until it wasn’t, and those owners are still waiting on an answer about upgrades. AI4 owners paid for the same promise.

And even if v15 drives well, I want to know how Tesla handles a chip failure with nobody behind the wheel. That’s not optional for Level 4. If the stack needs both SoCs to drive, what brings the car to a safe stop when one of them crashes?

In a recent development, as for v15 itself, I’m not drawing conclusions from influencer clips. Reality View looks great, but it’s also visibly laggy, and Musk admits it’s compute-limited. A great visual update is nice. Driving performance is what matters. I’ll wait until I get it in my own car to see how big the improvement actually is.

As soon as I started walking, I was playing a sport. I don’t remember there being a time where I wasn't on a sports team during my childhood. To me, exercise was practice after school and traveling for games on the weekend for whatever sport I was playing. As a teen, in my off-seasons, my mom would beg me to go to the gym with her for fun, but I didn't have much interest in it.

Industry observers note that I liked running and endurance-based activities because I felt like they complimented sports pretty well, especially lacrosse, which eventually became my main activity. I ended up being able to play lacrosse in college, where I was first required to start strength training to prepare for the season. While I was in shape for my sport, I couldn’t even lift the bar in the gym, and I was mesmerized by all the different movements that I didn’t really understand.

Recent findings suggest that in the middle of college, everyone was sent home because of the pandemic. I felt far away from my entire life and all my friends, and like there was nothing for me to be doing. There was so much time on my hands, and there was nowhere for me to be.

While sitting at home alone, I had nothing to do besides work out. To pass the time and cope with what was happening, I wanted to exercise, but I felt stuck since gyms were closed.

Sources indicate that then my dad handed me this 25-pound bag of rice from Costco and said, “You can train with this. There’s actually a lot you can do with it.” So I stuffed that bag of rice in a backpack to make it heavy, and I’d use it as a weight. I would put the backpack at the front of my body and do squats. I would use it as a kettlebell for kettlebell swings. I would put it on my back and do walking lunges.

It has been revealed that I realized there was a lot I could do at home, but I wanted to try to strength train at the actual gym. I decided that, when I was done playing college lacrosse, I would get serious about a gym routine.

It has been revealed that when I graduated from college, I was excited—but so confused—about where to begin. I followed fitness influencers on TikTok who gave workout tips and advice on which movements to try. But I also wanted to make sure all of my information was accurate and science-based, so I started researching online, watching the moves other people at the gym were doing, and reaching out to my old college coaches for tips.

It has been revealed that at first, I thought I needed to be running and lifting every day to stay fit, but I soon realized I was over-exerting my body. I started learning more about the basics of strength training and how to work different muscles with compound movements like squats, deadlifts, hang cleans, and more. I also learned how to supplement those movements by doing auxiliary exercises with dumbbells or body weight exercises like curls, lunges, and more.

After a combination of trial and error, researching, and practicing at the gym, I finally found my strength training routine and stride. I started to finally perfect my strength exercises. My confidence was growing so much as a result, which only motivated me to continue. I developed so much discipline that translated into every other aspect of my life.

Sources indicate that even when things got off-routine for me, I could fall back into strength training to find my rhythm again. I know it’ll always be there, giving me structure even when everything else feels unsettled.

When I first started lifting, I was hungrier because I was training more, but I was afraid to eat more. But if you want to build muscle, you need protein and you have to eat! It’s how your body survives and thrives. You need to take care of yourself, and that includes getting enough sleep.

According to recent reports, I do not always feel motivated to workout. That’s just how life is. But when I started strength training, I developed so much discipline. Even when I don’t have motivation, that discipline is there now, not just at the gym. Stick with it and allow that habit to form.

Industry observers note that it’s honestly true when they say that movement is medicine. When I'm taking care of my body, even if my mental headspace isn't in peak condition, I feel better after movement. It’s not all about hitting personal bests, either. (Though those certainly help!) I might tell myself, “I don't want to go to the gym today, but I will because I know it’s good for me.” Strength training gives me the confidence to know I can do anything I set my mind to.

Nowadays, I strength train four days a week, and I’ll also do a designated cardio day. I base my training on muscle groups.

Each workout will have a main exercise, such as a squat, bench press, or deadlift. Then, I pair them with auxiliary exercises like lunges, quad extensions, hamstring curls, rear delt flies, incline dumbbell bench presses, and more that target smaller muscles.

Sources indicate that I try to stay between four to five exercises per workout so I don't overdo it. I like to keep it simple when I write my workout plans. I’ll follow those plans for a certain number of weeks depending on my goals, then I’ll move on from there. I like to keep things interesting for myself to ensure I never get bored, because I want to be able to do this forever.

I used to not be able to hang clean the bar, and once I even dropped it on my knee and ruptured my bursa. It was all bruised, and I was so embarrassed. From then on, I had a real mental block with hang cleans. I told myself, “I’m never going to be able to do a lot of weight.”.

It has been revealed that years later, I decided it was about time I face my fear. I worked my way up to being able to put 25-pound plates on each side, coming out to about 100 pounds, depending on the bar. The more I practiced, the easier it became for me, and getting there was a huge milestone.

Recent findings suggest that any upper-body movements are especially empowering to me. Many people don’t think you can have impressive upper-body strength as a woman. When I was able to work my way up to putting a 45-pound weight on each side for bench presses, coming out to 135 pounds, I felt unstoppable. It was such a big deal to me since I never thought I’d be able to do it. It’s such an empowering feeling to be doing something that a lot of people see as something only men would do.

#155724. Why Couldn’t I Be Happy for Someone I Love?

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

Why Couldn’t I Be Happy for Someone I Love?

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (890 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 26, 2026 | Reviewed by Kaja Perina.
  • This article was written in collaboration with Anna Goldfarb, author of Modern Friendship.
  • With the holidays upon us, many of us will gather with loved ones, sharing platefuls of food, laughter, and crucial updates about our lives.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 26, 2026 | Reviewed by Kaja Perina.

This article was written in collaboration with Anna Goldfarb, author of Modern Friendship.

With the holidays upon us, many of us will gather with loved ones, sharing platefuls of food, laughter, and crucial updates about our lives. If you’re recently engaged, expecting, or have received an impressive accolade at work, what better time to announce the news than when you’re all in the same room?

But hearing someone’s good news can be unexpectedly fraught, especially if you’re struggling. You might want to rejoice for them but find you can’t. By understanding why good news is uniquely powerful in making or breaking a relationship, you can navigate the holidays with self-compassion and avoid a sting from swelling into something bigger.

In a recent development, when we receive a friend’s bad news, we learn where we stand in their life. Finding out about our friend’s surgery through the grapevine, for example, reveals something about the closeness of the bond: the earlier we’re told, the closer we feel to that friend.

Industry observers note that if you find out you’re not in their inner circle of confidantes, it can make you question how close your friendship even was: “Fluffy died, and you didn’t tell me? Am I even your best friend?”.

According to recent reports, good news reveals closeness too. Researchers call it a norm of close friendship to share good news, so when we don’t, our friends may question how close we are. When we hide good news from others, research finds, they report feeling more insulted and less close to us.

Hearing that a dear friend is engaged, expecting, or has scored a promotion reshapes how we think about our own experience. While we may have felt at peace with our job title, hearing that a friend got promoted may make us suddenly feel inadequate. We compare our friend’s newly achieved status to our own, and make inferences regarding our value. Good news, then, forces us to confront our status.

Of course, this doesn’t happen all the time. If someone else’s positive news is in an area you don’t identify with, you can revel in their success. Your friend can win an award for being the best baker in the tri-state area. If you don’t care about being an elite baker, cheering them on doesn’t require you to measure yourself against them. However, if you also dream of being an accomplished baker, it will be much harder to be happy for them because of what their good news means for you.

Abraham Tesser’s Self-Evaluation Maintenance Model (1988) explains this well. His model predicts that when someone close to you outperforms you in an area central to who you are and what you care about, the comparison uniquely stings. That’s why we might take someone’s good news personally.

Here are two questions to help you figure out why you couldn’t be happy for someone when you wanted to be:.

Answers to the first question are usually:.

Each feeling points to a source.

Answers to the second question can reveal common closeness and status concerns:.

I wasn’t told when I expected to be.

I felt unimportant to my friend.

I wasn’t sure what it meant for me moving forward.

I felt less content with my own life.

Recent findings suggest that sometimes the answer is simpler: I wanted it for myself. That’s envy, and it’s normal.

It has been revealed that as you hear happy updates from others this holiday season, be gentle with yourself, as you might’ve just learned something fresh about your relationship with the other person. It’s normal to have complicated feelings in the moment.

Industry observers note that if you felt excluded because you weren’t told when you expected to be, start by celebrating their news, if you can. Later, you can let them know you’d love to hear updates sooner: “I love hearing your news. I hope you know you can always come to me with things like this.” Opening the conversation this way will hopefully give you more insight into their thinking. It also helps to reflect on who heard first and why. Do those people play a bigger role in your friend’s life right now? Are there sensible reasons your friend told other people first? Perhaps this friend shares work updates with you, but keeps personal updates to another circle. Now you know how they regard your relationship, and you can recalibrate your expectations.

If you felt inadequate after hearing the news, you’ll probably need some time and space to process the jolt. For example, if your friend is having a baby and you’ve recently had a miscarriage, you can tell your friend, “I’m so happy for you, and I need a little time to take it in. I’ll call you this weekend.” If you simply wanted the thing for yourself, own it: I wanted that job. Envy points to something you want, and you can still show up warmly while the envious feeling settles.

By understanding why you’re struggling to be happy for people you love, you give yourself the best chance of keeping the relationship once the feelings pass.

Toyota is overhauling its best-selling vehicle of all time, which will include the first fully electric Corolla.

The Toyota Corolla is one of the most recognized and best-selling automotive nameplates of all time.

Since its debut in 1966, over 57 million drivers have chosen the Corolla thanks to its reliability, low cost of ownership, efficiency, and affordable price tag.

Toyota sells the Corolla in more than 150 countries and has expanded the lineup over the past 50 years from sedans and hatchbacks to coupes, wagons, a sporty GR Corolla, and the Corolla Cross compact SUV.

For its 13th generation, Toyota is planning a major overhaul that’s expected to be its biggest transformation yet.

The next-gen Toyota Corolla will be based on a new “multipathway” platform that will support gas, hybrid, plug-in hybrid, and, for the first time, fully electric powertrains.

“Whether it’s a battery EV, plug-in hybrid, hybrid, or internal combustion engine vehicle ― whatever the power source ― let’s make good-looking cars that everyone will want to drive!” Toyota’s former president and current CEO Koji Sato stated after unveiling the Corolla Concept at the Japan Mobility Show last October.

Toyota has kept most details a secret, including battery and powertrain specs. However, the fresh version is expected to adopt a similar design to the concept.

“When we created the concept, we wanted to give the Corolla name a new twist,” Norihiko Kobayashi, who has led the Corolla program since 2011, told Motor.es during a recent interview.

The Corolla has undergone several minor updates over the past 60 years, but the next-gen model will look nothing like its predecessors.

“It wasn’t simply about following in the footsteps of the past,” Kobayashi explained, “we wanted to delve into the future while still maintaining the Corolla identity.”.

Developing the next-gen Corolla “wasn’t just about making a upcoming car, but about redefining the future without looking back,” he added.

Like the current version, the new Toyota Corolla will come in several different body types, including a sedan, hatchback, crossover, and a GR variant.

Recent findings suggest that the car is designed to offer all types of drivetrain - meaning that it is not optimized for any one of them. This means it will have more cost and less structural stiffness than if it were EV only.

Details have yet to be confirmed, but the Toyota Corolla EV is expected to be available in single- and dual-motor configurations and offer a pure electric driving range of at least 250 miles.

In a recent development, the hybrid will reportedly use a new 1.5-liter four-cylinder engine and an electric motor. Toyota’s engineers told Car and Driver the hybrid system would deliver around 134 horsepower. It’s also estimated to be 10% to 20% more efficient than the current Corolla.

In a recent development, toyota’s next-gen Corolla is expected to debut sometime in 2027 as a 2028 model year. According to Car and Driver, the gas version will likely start at around $25,000, the hybrid around $27,000, and the EV and PHEVs will likely be priced in the $30,000 range.

Earlier this month, the next-gen Toyota Corolla Cross was spotted testing for the first time (see the images here).

#155722. Plant-Based Milk Alternatives May Not Give You Enough Iodine. Here’s Why That Matters

📅 09 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (726 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Healthline ↗ Open Full Page

Plant-Based Milk Alternatives May Not Give You Enough Iodine. Here’s Why That Matters

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (726 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Replacing dairy with plant-based alternatives (PBAs), even partially, could substantially lower iodine intake, especially if those alternatives aren’t fortified, according to a recent study published in the Lancet Planetary Health.
  • Recent findings suggest that the United Kingdom-based researchers found that only 12% of UK plant-based milk, yogurt, and cheese products analyzed were fortified with iodine.
  • In the United States, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) provides guidance on the nutritional content of PBAs, but fortification with iodine is voluntary.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Replacing dairy with plant-based alternatives (PBAs), even partially, could substantially lower iodine intake, especially if those alternatives aren’t fortified, according to a recent study published in the Lancet Planetary Health.

Recent findings suggest that the United Kingdom-based researchers found that only 12% of UK plant-based milk, yogurt, and cheese products analyzed were fortified with iodine. This compares with 61% for calcium and 46% for vitamin B12.

In the United States, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) provides guidance on the nutritional content of PBAs, but fortification with iodine is voluntary.

The study found that replacing as little as 20% of dairy intake with plant-based alternatives could increase the risk of inadequate iodine intake, particularly among adolescent girls and women of reproductive age.

According to recent reports, “People often worry about a decline in calcium intake when they replace some of their dairy with plant-based alternatives. As a result, iodine is frequently overlooked. This study serves as a valuable reminder of iodine’s significance as a nutrient,” stated Victoria Finn, MD, board certified endocrinologist at Medical Offices of Manhattan, who wasn’t involved in the study.

The study included analysis of UK plant-based milk, cheese, and yogurt products, as well as dietary data from 3,500 people.

The researchers used statistical modeling to predict how swapping dairy for PBAs might affect iodine and other nutrients.

The people who are most vulnerable to iodine inadequacy are adolescent females and people at reproductive age, especially those who are pregnant or who blueprint to become pregnant.

The researchers estimated that replacing 20% to 35% of dairy intake with PBAs would increase the proportion of people with inadequate iodine intake:.

According to recent reports, when the researchers modeled the replacement of all dairy products with PBAs, the proportion of adolescent females with inadequate iodine intake rose to 80%. Among females ages 19 to 49, that proportion remained relatively stable as replacement rates increased.

It is crucial to keep in mind that the study used dietary modeling rather than direct measurement of iodine status.

Iodine is important for thyroid hormone production, metabolism, and both fetal and child brain development.

“Your thyroid gland requires iodine to produce thyroid hormones, which play a crucial role in regulating metabolism and supporting normal growth and development,” said Finn.

Industry observers note that she added that if you consistently consume too little iodine over an extended period, the thyroid gland may enlarge and eventually struggle to produce enough hormones. This condition is known as hypothyroidism, which can lead to various symptoms such as lethargy, sleepiness, weight gain, dry skin, and more.

“Hypothyroidism can be particularly dangerous during pregnancy, as the baby’s brain, nervous system, and organs rely heavily on the mother’s thyroid hormone during the early stages of development,” Finn added.

In the United Kingdom, dairy is a major iodine source due to cattle feed supplementation, not because dairy is naturally high in iodine.

In the United States, dairy is also an important source of iodine for the same reasons.

However, the risk profile for iodine deficiency in the U.S. may differ from the U.K., as iodized salt is also a significant source of iodine and is widely available in the U.S., but not in the U.K.

According to the National Institutes of Health (NIH), the recommended daily intake of iodine depends on your age.

It has been revealed that plant-based or plant-forward diets have grown in popularity, in part due to the health benefits they offer. For example, consuming less meat can reduce your risk of heart disease, type 2 diabetes, obesity, and high cholesterol.

In a recent development, however, as this study suggests, it may be possible to reduce your iodine intake when transitioning to a plant-based diet. There are ways you can protect your iodine intake when choosing a more plant-forward diet, though.

Check the labels on plant-based dairy alternatives to find those fortified with iodine. You can also read the nutrition label. Iodine may be listed as potassium iodide or potassium iodate.

Seafood, eggs, and iodized salt are all good sources of iodine.

You can also discuss iodine supplements with your healthcare professional.

In a recent development, “Iodine supplements should be taken with caution, especially without checking your thyroid levels,” said Finn. “Additionally, be cautious with kelp supplements, as their iodine content can vary, and excessive iodine intake can disrupt thyroid function.”.

What Teachers Know (Or Don’t Know) About Left-Handedness

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (721 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 26, 2026 | Reviewed by Kaja Perina.
  • It has been revealed that all over the world, teachers play a crucial role in their pupils' learning experience.
  • It has been revealed that A upcoming study entitled “Handedness literacy in teachers: Data from Greece, Serbia, and Belgium”, just published in the scientific journal Laterality, aimed at closing this gap in the psychological literature by focusing on teachers’ handedness literacy (Papadatou-Pastou and co-workers, 2026).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 26, 2026 | Reviewed by Kaja Perina.

It has been revealed that all over the world, teachers play a crucial role in their pupils' learning experience. This is especially true for left-handed children, who, for a long time, have been forced to write with their right hand against their will in many countries. Thankfully, the awful practice of handedness relearning is now a thing of the past in the US and many other countries, and today, both left-handed and right-handed pupils are encouraged to write with their naturally dominant hand in school. This makes it key that teachers have some basic knowledge about handedness and also the ergonomic needs of left-handed kids in learning environments. As handedness typically is not a main focus in teacher education, it is, however, largely unknown what knowledge the average teacher has about handedness and the specific learning needs of left-handed children. Thus, more psychological research on this important topic is needed.

It has been revealed that A upcoming study entitled “Handedness literacy in teachers: Data from Greece, Serbia, and Belgium”, just published in the scientific journal Laterality, aimed at closing this gap in the psychological literature by focusing on teachers’ handedness literacy (Papadatou-Pastou and co-workers, 2026). Handedness literacy refers to a person’s general knowledge and understanding of handedness.

Industry observers note that the study team, led by renowned handedness researcher Marietta Papadatou-Pastou, asked more than 800 prospective and in-service teachers to fill out a questionnaire with various questions about their knowledge of handedness and about themselves. The teachers came from three different European countries: Greece, Serbia, and Belgium.

Sources indicate that the questionnaire the teachers had to fill out consisted of four main parts. The first part consisted of open-ended questions about left-handedness, such as “Do left-handed students differ from right-handed students?”. The teachers had to write answers to these questions. The second part of the questionnaire consisted of 18 questions quizzing the teachers about their knowledge of handedness. The third part of the questionnaire contained further questions about handedness, and the fourth part contained some questions about the teachers themselves, such as their own handedness and their age, among others.

The analysis of the data yielded several interesting results about teachers’ handedness literacy.

In a recent development, the analyses of the open-ended questions about handedness in the first part of the questionnaire showed that teachers generally had a supportive attitude towards left-handed pupils. The teachers wrote about different aspects of handedness, such as the underlying neurobiology or specific challenges left-handed pupils face, or their ergonomic and classroom needs. In general, they were in favor of letting children choose which hand they like to write with.

The analysis of the handedness literacy scores revealed that teachers knew some things about handedness, but also had quite a lot of knowledge gaps. As there were 18 questions and the scientists gave 1 point per correct question, the maximum score for handedness literacy was 18. Teachers from Serbia had an average score of 8.11 (45% correct answers). Teachers from Belgium were slightly better as they had an average score of 8.85 (49% correct answers), as were teachers from Greece, who had an average score of 8.90 (49% correct answers).

Industry observers note that so, in all three countries, teachers had less than 50% correct answers- if there were a left-handedness test, they would probably fail! One thing that many teachers got wrong was that they thought that left-handed pupils were more intelligent than right-handed pupils. Also, many teachers thought that there were more left-handers in the population than the actual percentage (10.6%). Interestingly, left-handed teachers did not show higher handedness literacy than right-handed teachers.

According to recent reports, many of the teachers who participated in the study stated that they thought that handedness literacy in teachers needs to be improved. The results of the study show that this is actually true. This suggests that teacher education should include more scientific information on left-handedness, so that teachers can optimally educate left-handed kids.

Papadatou-Pastou, M., Papadopoulou, A. K., Kovic, V., Gerrits, R., & Vingerhoets, G. (2026). Handedness literacy in teachers: Data from Greece, Serbia, and Belgium. Laterality, 1–43. Advance online publication. https://doi.org/10.1080/1357650X.2026.2753053.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two large studies published on November 5 link declining newborn vitamin K shot rates to a sharp increase in infant bleeding cases, including potentially fatal brain hemorrhages.

A research letter, published in JAMA Pediatrics, analyzed data on approximately 11 million infants from 2017 to 2025 and found that vitamin K administration declined from 97.7% to 95%, while cases of vitamin K deficiency bleeding (VKDB) nearly quadrupled.

In a recent development, A second study published in JAMA, based on data from 5.2 million U.S. infants, found that refusal rates more than doubled, rising from 3.1% in 2017 to 6.8% in 2025. Infants who did not receive the shot had a 47% higher risk of bleeding and more than twice the risk of intracranial bleeding.

Additionally, new data from Truveta suggest the trend is continuing: refusals of vitamin K shots increased by 57% between January and June 2026, rising from 5.2% to 8.1% of newborns.

Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting, and newborns naturally have very low levels. Without the preventive injection, infants are at risk for VKDB, which can cause sudden bleeding in the brain, gastrointestinal tract, and other organs. Late-onset VKDB can occur up to six months after birth, often without warning signs, and may be fatal.

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) continue to recommend an intramuscular vitamin K injection for all newborns, ideally within 6 hours of birth.

In a recent development, the shot is not a vaccine; it is a nutrient injection that helps prevent dangerous bleeding. A single dose reduces the risk of late-onset VKDB by approximately 98%.

Experts not involved in the studies attribute the rise in refusals partly to broader vaccine hesitancy and mixed public health messaging.

“The decision to vaccinate a newborn or allow a vitamin K injection at birth is complex, with multiple factors playing a role in the ultimate decision,” stated Graham Tse, MD, a pediatrician and chief medical officer of MemorialCare Miller Children’s & Women’s Hospital in Long Beach, CA.

According to recent reports, some of these factors, Tse remarked, include conflicting messages from federal health agencies such as the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), both overseen by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., an outspoken critic of the childhood immunization schedule.

According to recent reports, the vitamin K shot is not a vaccine, yet RFK Jr. has declined to reassure parents about its safety, despite the CDC’s current recommendation to administer it at birth.

Additionally, growing medical distrust among parents has led to refusal of routine newborn care, such as the vitamin K shot, Reuters reports.

Healthline spoke with Tse to learn more about the risks of refusing the vitamin K shot and what upcoming or expectant parents should know about this routine newborn treatment.

This interview has been lightly edited and condensed for clarity and length.

Tse: The decision to vaccinate a newborn or allow a vitamin K injection at birth is complex, with multiple factors playing a role in the ultimate decision.

A contributing factor to the decline in vitamin K injection at birth, as well as in newborn hepatitis B vaccination, is the conflicting messages from the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Recommendations from these entities and others are conflicting or do not align with established, research-based, and proven recommendations from organizations such as the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) and the Infectious Diseases Society of America.

When there are conflicting recommendations, it creates confusion and doubt among parents about what the best or right choice is for their child.

As well, there is so much misinformation on the internet, among influencers, and on social media that it is difficult to know what information is accurate, well-researched, and proven, versus what may be just someone’s opinion or belief.

In a recent development, some are mistaking the vitamin K injection at birth for a vaccination, which it is not. Ultimately, all these factors are contributing to parents declining or delaying vitamin K injections at birth.

In a recent development, tse: Declining the newborn vitamin K injection puts the newborn at significant risk of serious and life threatening complications from vitamin K-deficient bleeding (VKDB). This was previously referred to as hemorrhagic disease of the newborn.

VKDB can be as mild as bruising of the skin but can be as serious as bleeding into the brain, and newborns and infants can die from VKDB.

Declining vitamin K injection at birth is significant because of the serious and potentially life threatening consequences of deficiency of Vitamin K and not being able to clot the blood.

The vitamin K injection at birth is highly effective at preventing VKDB.

Tse: If a neonate or infant has vitamin K deficiency, the ability to clot their blood and stop bleeding is highly reduced.

All newborns are at risk of low vitamin K due to low body stores, low vitamin K content of breast milk, reduced ability of the gut to mobilize vitamin K, and poor transfer of vitamin K across the placenta.

Sources indicate that when the blood cannot clot, bleeding from minor or minimal trauma can occur, and even bleeding without injury or trauma may occur. This can include bruises, bleeding from the mouth or gastrointestinal tract, bleeding from cuts or circumcision.

Bleeding can occur anywhere in the body, including in the brain, which can be catastrophic.

VKDB can occur from birth and through several months of life. Bleeding in the brain from VKDB, one of the most serious consequences, can occur at any time from birth to up to 6 months or so and can occur unexpectedly and suddenly. Vitamin K given at birth can prevent this risk of bleeding.

Sources indicate that tse: Vitamin K is a necessary vitamin that all humans need. Vitamin K is not a vaccination.

Newborns need vitamin K to prevent serious, significant, and often catastrophic bleeding during their first several months of life.

Vitamin K has been given to newborns in the United States for close to 70 years, is safe, is studied, and is proven to help prevent vitamin K-deficient bleeding.

I urge new parents to allow their newborns to receive the vitamin K injection at birth — it protects them, keeps them healthy, is proven safe, and is recommended.

In a recent development, A little backstory is helpful here. After Saab Automobile closed its doors in 2012 following an ill-fated tie-up with Spyker, a Chinese consortium called National Electric Vehicle Sweden (NEVS) acquired the majority of the remaining assets, including the Trollhättan factory, manufacturing equipment and intellectual property. However, NEVS was not interested in building a next-generation Saab 9-3 Aero. Instead, they had their sights set on building an electric car future.

It has been revealed that their vision of that was called the Emily GT, envisioned as a sophisticated electric grand touring sedan capable of competing with established luxury EVs. Development began in late 2019, and just 10 months later, the Emily GT rolled out into view. And much like Saabs of the past, the Emily GT had some unique features—the most obvious being its four electric motors, one mounted inside each wheel. Combined, they produced a healthy 490 horsepower.

According to recent reports, however, while the power output was healthy, the financial condition of the organization was not. NEVS never secured the funding necessary to bring the car into production. The ambitious project remained stuck in the prototype stage, where it’s stayed frozen .

So, do you think you’re the right person to bring it to market? If so—or even if you’d rather just own a very odd automotive dead-end—Klaravik will open online bidding on November 25, with the auction scheduled to conclude December 9. All four completed vehicles and the accompanying development materials are being offered together rather than individually.

Sources indicate that of course, buying the prototypes and engineering materials doesn't automatically give someone a functioning car firm or guarantee a path to production. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 26, 2026 | Reviewed by Kaja Perina.
  • It has been revealed that have you ever met a newly introduced friend who seemed to think you were too great?
  • Idealization and devaluation like this are two sides of the same coin—splitting, which is most associated with borderline personality disorder, or BPD.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 26, 2026 | Reviewed by Kaja Perina.

It has been revealed that have you ever met a newly introduced friend who seemed to think you were too great? You can do no wrong, you’re the first person to ever truly understand them, you’re so much better than their other friends. But then you have a disagreement or miss a birthday party, and they seem to just…turn on you? Now they feel sure that you were only ever kind to them because you wanted something; you’re just like everyone else.

Idealization and devaluation like this are two sides of the same coin—splitting, which is most associated with borderline personality disorder, or BPD. But it, or behaviors that closely resemble it, can also occur in people with narcissistic traits, depression, anxiety, autism, and other conditions. In fact, we all do it to some degree; teenagers are notorious for it. And it happens in all kinds of relationships: friendship, family, professional, marriage or partnership.

Sources indicate that obviously, neither extreme is a complete or fair perception of you. The truth of who you are exists somewhere between the ideal and the devalued, but that liminal space isn’t something your friend has access to right now.

And within that inability to see the space between all-good and all-bad lies the definition of splitting. In all of us, certain cognitive processes go offline when we become dysregulated or lose homeostasis: You don’t communicate well when you’re hungry, you can’t appreciate the beauty of a sunset when you’re angry, and so on. Likewise, when your friend or loved one becomes triggered and splits, their ability to see the nuance of who you are goes offline.

According to recent reports, in a way, you each experience a similar betrayal. You’re late coming home from work, and by the time you arrive, your spouse’s overactive threat detection network has them convinced you’re seeing someone else. You don’t really love them. You’ll probably leave. You’re abandoning them.

It has been revealed that of course that’s not what you’re doing. So, you’re likewise blindsided by their response. Your spouse is fuming because you betrayed them, and they have some choice words for you. Every positive aspect of your relationship is read back to you in a negative light. It feels like they hate you.

There is no law that notes you must stay in a relationship with this dynamic. However, if you’re committed to it, then equanimity is paramount. Your key to coping is not to internalize either idealization or devaluation. Even though it feels so personal, it’s not about you. It’s about their pain and fear.

According to recent reports, it may help to think of splitting as a halted developmental process. Children learn good and bad first, and then they come to understand nuance later. But that learning can be disrupted by a number of childhood experiences, including:.

When a person’s emotional development was disrupted in this way, their brain is quick to interpret small things as threats, such as:.

It has been revealed that it’s not willful, and that’s important for any person who loves someone with BPD to know. In most cases, people with borderline personality disorder experienced feeling chronically unsafe, uncared for, or unseen during an important developmental stage. Their brain is hyper-wired to detect this type of threat and respond defensively.

You’re under no obligation to engage in any relationship that doesn’t work for you. You decide what’s okay for you, and it’s a neutral choice. No one has to be right or wrong. And if a relationship ever involves threats or physical harm, that crosses a line no diagnosis excuses. Leave the situation and get help right away.

Industry observers note that if you’re safe and you choose to stay involved: First, know that borderline personality disorder is highly treatable. Recovery and remission are possible and even likely with the right support. And there are a few things you can do to take care of yourself and support your loved one. For you:.

And to support your loved one in feeling safe and secure so that they may recover:.

In a recent development, learned safety can rewire the fear that leads to splitting. As people with BPD build a sense of safety in treatment and in trustworthy relationships, the space between all-good and all-bad slowly and increasingly opens up to them.

#155711. A rare triple-star system near Earth ‘should not exist’

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (513 w)

A rare triple-star system near Earth ‘should not exist’

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (513 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Astronomers searching for new exoplanets recently found something much stranger—a rarely seen triple-star system located only 28 light-years away from Earth.
  • Recent findings suggest that “The system should not exist,” Patrick Dufour, a University of Montreal astrophysicist and study co-author, mentioned in a statement.
  • Dufour’s team first noticed the perplexing triple-star system while scanning for exoplanets using highly sensitive equipment mounted on the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope near the dormant volcano of Mauna Kea.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Astronomers searching for new exoplanets recently found something much stranger—a rarely seen triple-star system located only 28 light-years away from Earth. If that weren’t odd enough, two of its three stellar components are dense, depleted white dwarfs. A study recently published in the Astronomy & Astrophysics Journal details an oddball trio that is so perplexing that researchers still aren’t quite sure how it formed in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that “The system should not exist,” Patrick Dufour, a University of Montreal astrophysicist and study co-author, mentioned in a statement. “We have no clean explanation for how it got here.”.

Dufour’s team first noticed the perplexing triple-star system while scanning for exoplanets using highly sensitive equipment mounted on the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope near the dormant volcano of Mauna Kea. Astronomers were specifically looking for subtle discrepancies in the movements of distant stars, which often indicates that there are orbiting planets nearby.

It has been revealed that but when it came to one particular red dwarf, the data simply didn’t make sense. Rather than delicate shifts in motion, researchers recorded velocity swings at speeds nearing 10 miles per second. This effect was too much for a single planet to cause, and after years of additional observations, astronomers determined that whatever the unseen subject was, it possessed a mass greater than half the sun.

“The object’s unusual combination of high mass and dim light left only one plausible explanation: it was the remains of a dead star,” explained Charles-Antoine Parent, a University of Montreal astronomer and study co-author.

Possible suspects included a neutron star and even a secret black hole, but some assistance from the Gemini North telescope also on Mauna Kea finally confirmed its identity: a close-orbiting white dwarf. This complicated the situation. Astronomers previously discovered another white dwarf circling the red dwarf at a much greater distance. Taken altogether, that made three stars existing in a single system. The grouping is now known as Welopō‘ai, a Hawaiian phrase that roughly translates to “path of family traits” in reference to the stars’ shared relationships. According to researchers, no other comparable example can be found within 100 light-years of Earth.

In a recent development, however, Welopō‘ai still doesn’t quite add up. The red dwarf’s nearest companion was about 40 percent more massive than our sun prior to transforming into a white dwarf. When it did, it would have expanded hundreds of times its original size. Previously documented systems featuring these dynamics entailed the two stars falling into an even tighter orbit, or even merging. Despite this, Welopō‘ai’s red dwarf is still there and in a strikingly stable, wide orbit with the closest white dwarf. The team now prepares to continue observing their discovery to learn as much as possible about the triple-star system, and possibly figure out how it formed in the first place.

“Discoveries like this remind us that our own cosmic neighborhood still contains remarkable surprises,” added study co-author and astronomer, Étienne Artigau.

BYD Ti7 banned from the EU for copying the Land Rover Defender’s design

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1078 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Dutch court has barred BYD from selling or building its Ti7 SUV anywhere in the European Union after ruling that it infringes Jaguar Land Rover’s registered design for the Land Rover Defender.
  • It’s a sharp turnaround from 10 days ago, when the same court in The Hague handed BYD an early win in the Defender copycat fight.
  • The preliminary relief judge at the District Court of The Hague issued the ruling on Friday, November 20, in summary proceedings JLR brought against 11 BYD companies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Dutch court has barred BYD from selling or building its Ti7 SUV anywhere in the European Union after ruling that it infringes Jaguar Land Rover’s registered design for the Land Rover Defender. Breaking the injunction costs BYD €100,000 per day, up to €10 million.

It’s a sharp turnaround from 10 days ago, when the same court in The Hague handed BYD an early win in the Defender copycat fight. BYD’s Hong Kong shares fell as much as 4% on Monday before closing 1.9% lower.

The preliminary relief judge at the District Court of The Hague issued the ruling on Friday, November 20, in summary proceedings JLR brought against 11 BYD companies.

JLR put six registered EU designs in front of the court. The judge only needed one of them: design 005248580-0004, registered in April 2018 and covering the current Defender 110, known internally as the L663.

According to the ruling, the elements that dominate that design are the rounded “shoulders,” the rounded corners, the signature panel on the C-pillar, the rounded wheel-arch cutouts, the continuous window line, and the overall silhouette. The court found every one of them on the Ti7.

Here’s how the two SUVs compare from the same angles, using official press images from BYD and JLR:.

Sources indicate that BYD argued that the headlights, grille, bumpers, hood and side profile are all different. Not enough, remarked the judge, who ruled that those differences, on their own or combined, don’t give an informed user a different overall impression. The court also found the Ti7 sits closer to the Defender than to older boxy SUVs like the Ford Flex, Jeep Wrangler and Mercedes G-Class.

BYD doesn’t sell the Ti7 in the EU. It told the court it has “no concrete aims” to launch it there and that the SUV can only be ordered in the UK.

The judge didn’t buy that as a defense. By BYD’s own account, it developed the seven-seat layout for the UK and Europe, a promotional video called the Ti7 the first seven-seat SUV “in Europe,” and BYD wouldn’t commit to keeping it out of the EU. That was enough for the court to find a threat of infringement.

Recent findings suggest that so BYD’s EU entities can no longer import, produce, offer, sell, store or supply the Ti7. The order kicks in one week after the ruling is formally served, and it even covers BYD’s Hungarian unit, since the judge considered it conceivable the Ti7 could come out of the new Szeged factory.

The UK is a different story. The court said it has no jurisdiction over BYD UK and threw out JLR’s UK design claims, so British deliveries are still on for January 2027. That’s the one European market where BYD actually opened orders, pricing the Ti7 at £47,995, about £24,000 below the £71,840 plug-in Defender 110.

BYD said it “strongly disagrees” with the judgment and will appeal, adding that the Ti7 “is the result of BYD’s own independent design work and infringes none of JLR’s rights.” JLR told AFP it protects its intellectual property and takes legal action when necessary.

Industry observers note that BYD has four weeks to appeal, but the injunction stays in force while it does. JLR, for its part, has six months to file a full case on the merits, or BYD can get the injunction lifted.

This whole thing started in August, when JLR had bailiffs raid BYD’s Dutch offices in Schiedam and Hoofddorp. The court later ordered JLR to destroy everything it seized, saying it didn’t need BYD’s internal files to make its design case. And it didn’t. JLR won on the design registration alone.

The Ti7 looks like a Defender. We said so when BYD first brought it to the UK, and so did pretty much everyone else. Chinese automakers have been building Defender lookalikes for years, but most of them stayed in China.

BYD brought one to the Defender’s home turf at a £24,000 discount, so a fight with JLR was always coming.

"...ruled that those differences, on their own or combined, don’t give an informed user a different overall impression.".

It has been revealed that really? I feel like anyone who pays even a little attention to car designs isn't going to mistake the two. The thing most people see as differentiating within the same category is the headlights, tail lights, grill - which are all significantly different.

The only real similarity is the proportions, there are a ton of similarly proportioned SUVs but that's a result of the form factor.

But honestly, all these boxy SUVs look the same to me.

Nobody owns “boxy.” JLR even failed to trademark the classic Defender’s shape in the UK, a fight it lost in its legal battle with the Ineos Grenadier. But it registered the new Defender’s design in 2018, and that specific combination of shoulders, C-pillar panel and wheel arches is exactly what the court protected. That’s how design rights are supposed to work.

Industry observers note that the actual business damage is small for now. The Ti7 sells roughly 30,000 units a month, almost all in China, and the UK launch goes ahead. The stock dip was about headlines more than lost Ti7 sales.
